items.title: US Hormuz blockade could cost Iran $435 million a day

featured_image.name: US military threatens to blockade all Iranian ports starting ...

items.description:
The United States naval blockade of Iranian ports, which took effect on Monday at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time, could inflict roughly $435 million in daily economic damage on Iran, according to an analysis first reported by The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The estimate, compiled by Miad Maleki, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and former official at the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control, breaks down to approximately $276 million per day in lost exports — primarily crude oil and petrochemicals — and $159 million per day in disrupted imports. In a detailed thread on X, Maleki noted the figures assume Iran exports 1.5 million barrels of oil daily at a wartime price of about $87 per barrel, with more than 90 per cent of that volume shipping through Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Amazon nears Globalstar acquisition to challenge Starlink

featured_image.name: Amazon nears deal to acquire Globalstar in push to rival Musk's ...

items.description: Amazon is on the verge of acquiring satellite operator Globalstar in a deal that could be announced as early as Tuesday, according to Bloomberg News, marking a dramatic escalation in the tech giant's push to compete with SpaceX's Starlink in the low-Earth orbit internet market.[1][2]

items.title: China lifts restrictions on some BHP iron ore purchases

featured_image.name: BHP achieves first ore at South Flank iron ore operation in ...

items.description:
China's state-backed iron ore buyer has told several steel mills they may resume purchasing some BHP cargoes, marking a thaw in a months-long commercial dispute that has roiled global iron ore markets. BHP shares rose on Tuesday following the news, reported first by Bloomberg.[1]

Officials from China Mineral Resources Group told plants they can resume bidding for some BHP cargoes denominated in U.S. dollars starting Tuesday, according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter. Mills have not yet been explicitly allowed to take physical deliveries from Chinese ports, but a notice is expected. Reuters separately confirmed that China has lifted bans on procurement of the steelmaking ingredient from BHP.[2][1]

items.title: BP expects 'exceptional' Q1 trading results from war-driven oil volatility

featured_image.name: Oil market gripped by record volatility and speculation since start of ...

items.description: BP said on Tuesday it expects its oil trading desk to deliver "exceptional" first-quarter results, as the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran sent crude prices surging and created the kind of volatile market conditions in which the company's traders thrive.[1][2]

items.title: OpenAI backers question $852B valuation amid strategy shifts

featured_image.name: OpenAI closes funding round at an $852 billion valuation - CNBC

items.description:
Some of OpenAI's own backers are questioning whether the company's $852 billion valuation can hold up as it pivots toward the enterprise market and contends with mounting competitive pressure from Anthropic and Google, according to a report by the Financial Times on Tuesday.[1]

The concerns come just weeks after OpenAI closed a $122 billion funding round — the largest in Silicon Valley history — led by Amazon, Nvidia, and SoftBank, with additional backing from Andreessen Horowitz, Abu Dhabi's MGX, and T. Rowe Price. Yet some investors told the Financial Times the company has redrawn its product roadmap twice in the past six months in response to competitive threats, first from Google and then from Anthropic, raising questions about strategic coherence ahead of a potential initial public offering later this year.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Chinese tanker transits Strait of Hormuz despite new U.S. blockade on Iran

featured_image.name: China Oil Tankers Break Out of Strait of Hormuz via Iran ‘Tollbooth’

items.description: The United States launched a naval blockade of Iranian ports on Monday, escalating a six-week-old conflict with Tehran after weekend peace talks collapsed — and within hours, a Chinese-owned tanker sailed through the Strait of Hormuz in apparent defiance of the operation, raising the specter of a broader confrontation between Washington and Beijing.

items.title: Carney's Liberals secure majority in Canadian by-elections

featured_image.name: How Mark Carney led Canada's Liberal Party to election win

items.description:
Prime Minister Mark Carney's Liberal Party secured a parliamentary majority on Monday after voters in three by-elections in Ontario and Quebec delivered the seats needed to push the party past the 172-seat threshold in the 343-seat House of Commons.[1][2][3]

The Liberals entered the day holding 171 seats, meaning a single victory in any of the three contested ridings — Scarborough Southwest, University-Rosedale, and Terrebonne — would clinch the majority. Polls had shown the party favored to win at least two of the three.[4][2][5][1]

items.title: Trump rejects Iran's 5-year enrichment offer as ceasefire deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Iran with bombs unless nuclear deal reached

items.description: Iran formally responded on Monday to a U.S. demand that it freeze uranium enrichment for 20 years, offering instead to suspend enrichment activities for up to five years, according to two senior Iranian officials and a U.S. official cited by The New York Times. President Trump rejected the proposal, deepening the impasse between Washington and Tehran as a ceasefire deadline looms on April 21.[1][2][3]

items.title: Aalto team traps light on a chip for millions of cycles

featured_image.name: A new, low-cost, high-efficiency photonic integrated circuit

items.description: Researchers at Aalto University have developed a fabrication technique that allows atomically thin materials to trap light on a chip for millions of cycles, a result they say surpasses previous performance by three orders of magnitude. The work, published in Nature Materials on April 13, was carried out by an international team and addresses one of the longest-standing barriers in the development of photonic chips built from so-called van der Waals materials.[1][2]

items.title: Vance says ball is in Iran's court as US naval blockade takes effect

featured_image.name: The U.S. military says it will blockade Iranian ports as Iran peace talks collapse

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance said Monday that the next move in U.S.-Iran peace negotiations rests with Tehran, as a naval blockade on Iranian ports took effect following the collapse of weekend talks in Islamabad.

"The ball is very much in their court," Vance told Fox News anchor Bret Baier on "Special Report." "You ask what happens next, I think the Iranians are going to determine what happens next."[1][2]

items.title: Israeli airstrikes kill four in Gaza as Cairo talks stall

featured_image.name: White House announces "phase two" of Gaza ceasefire deal - Axios

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike killed at least three Palestinians in the central Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials said, even as mediators from Egypt, Turkey, and Qatar met with Hamas and other Palestinian faction leaders in Cairo in an effort to advance a stalled ceasefire deal.[1][2]

The strike hit a group of men outside a school in Deir al-Balah, according to medics. There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military. At Al-Aqsa Hospital, relatives arrived to bid farewell to the dead, their bodies laid in white shrouds outside the morgue. "This isn't a truce; it's a trap for our young men. Every day there are martyrs, every single day," said Umm Hussam Abu El-Rous, a relative of one of the victims, according to Reuters.[2][1]

items.title: US offered Iran 20-year enrichment freeze as talks collapsed

featured_image.name: U.S. and Iran tout progress in nuclear talks as supreme ...

items.description: The United States asked Iran to accept a 20-year moratorium on uranium enrichment during weekend negotiations in Islamabad, marking a shift from Washington's earlier demand that Tehran permanently abandon enrichment on its soil, according to The Wall Street Journal and Axios. Iran rejected the proposal, countering with a far shorter "single-digit" timeframe, and the marathon talks ended without a deal after 21 hours.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Israeli troops fire tear gas at schoolchildren in West Bank

featured_image.name: Israeli troops fire tear gas at Palestinian schoolchildren ...

items.description:
Israeli forces fired tear gas at Palestinian schoolchildren staging a sit-in in the occupied West Bank on Monday, according to AFP footage from the scene, as students attempted to return to class for the first time in more than 40 days.[1][2]

The incident took place at Umm al-Khair, a small village in the southern West Bank region of Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron. Israeli settlers from the nearby Carmel settlement had erected a barbed wire fence overnight blocking the road to the village school, preventing students and residents from reaching it.[3][1]

items.title: Trump says Iran called seeking deal after blockade began

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes US is close to reaching a new Iran ...

items.description:
Hours after a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports took effect Monday morning, President Trump told reporters outside the White House that Iran had reached out to his administration about resuming peace negotiations. "We've been called by the other side," Trump said. "They'd like to make a deal. Very badly, very badly."[1]

The blockade, which began at 10 a.m. EDT, applies to all vessels navigating to and from Iranian ports on the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, according to U.S. Central Command, though ships heading to non-Iranian ports through the Strait of Hormuz would not be impeded. Trump warned that any Iranian ships approaching the blockade would be "immediately ELIMINATED."[2][1]

items.title: Chinese AI solves decade-old math problem in 80 hours

featured_image.name: Peking University AI Solves Open Math Conjecture (Source ...

items.description: A team from Peking University has developed an artificial intelligence system that independently solved and verified an open mathematical conjecture first posed more than a decade ago by an American mathematician — completing the work in roughly 80 hours without any human mathematical judgment, according to a preprint paper published on April 4 on the arXiv repository.[1][2]

items.title: JWST finds strongest evidence yet for universe's first stars

featured_image.name: James Webb Space Telescope May Have Spotted the Universe's ...

items.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have uncovered what may be the most compelling evidence to date for Population III stars — the theoretical first generation of stars to form in the universe. The findings, detailed in two companion studies published as preprints on the arXiv server, center on a small, faint object called Hebe, located near one of the earliest known galaxies, GN-z11, which existed just 400 million years after the Big Bang.[1][2]

items.title: Iran says it hasn't charged Indian ships tolls as U.S. blockade takes effect

featured_image.name: Two India-Bound Tankers Pass Through Strait Of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran's ambassador to India declared on Monday that Tehran has not charged Indian vessels any tolls for transiting the Strait of Hormuz, seeking to reassure New Delhi of continued support even as a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports took effect the same day.

"You can ask the Indian government if we have charged anything up to now," Ambassador Mohammad Fathali told reporters at a briefing at Iran's embassy in New Delhi, according to Reuters. "In this difficult time, we have good relations. We believe Iran and India share common interests and a common fate."[1]

items.title: US begins naval blockade of Iranian ports after peace talks collapse

featured_image.name: Oil prices surge above $100 as U.S. Navy to blockade Iran's ports after peace talks fail

items.description: The United States military began enforcing a naval blockade of all Iranian ports on Monday at 10 a.m. Eastern Time, a dramatic escalation in the six-week conflict that came after marathon peace negotiations in Pakistan ended without a deal over the weekend.

items.title: Trump warns Iran 'fast-attack' ships near blockade will be 'eliminated'

featured_image.name: Trump Says Iranian 'Fast-attack' Ships that Come Close to US ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump warned on Monday that any Iranian "fast-attack" ships approaching the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports would be "immediately eliminated," escalating a confrontation with Tehran just as the blockade took effect in the Strait of Hormuz.

"Iran's Navy is laying at the bottom of the sea, completely obliterated — 158 ships," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "What we have not hit are their small number of, what they call, 'fast attack ships,' because we did not consider them much of a threat." He added that any such vessels approaching the blockade would be destroyed "using the same system of kill that we use against the drug dealers on boats at Sea. It is quick and brutal."[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Ship traffic halts in Strait of Hormuz as U.S. blockade begins

featured_image.name: What a US-led Hormuz strait naval blockade would look like ...

items.description:
Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz appeared to halt on Monday after President Donald Trump announced on social media that the United States would blockade the critical waterway, sending oil prices surging and deepening a global energy crisis triggered by weeks of conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran.

Lloyd's List Intelligence reported that ships had stopped moving through the strait, while Brent crude surged more than 8 percent to above $103 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude jumped roughly 8 percent past $104. Wholesale gasoline prices spiked 6 percent and heating oil climbed 10 percent in early trading.[1][2][3][4][5]
